---
title: "Excel, PowerPoint, Word and interactive tables"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r}
library(phwstyle)
library(dplyr)
set.seed(1)
dat <- tibble(group = sample(c("Group A", "Group B", "Group C"), 300, replace = TRUE),
              type = sample(c("Type 1", "Type 2", "Type 3"), 300, replace = TRUE),
              year = sample(2024:2025, 300, replace = TRUE))
tab <- phw_group_table(dat, c(group, type), year)
```

## Excel

`phw_write_xlsx()` writes one sheet per table, with a title, a navy
header, number formats, frozen headers and the source underneath. Summary
tables keep their bold group rows and indents.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
phw_write_xlsx(list(Grouped = tab, Raw = dat), "tables.xlsx",
               title = c("Counts by group and type", "Raw data"), source = "Example data")
```

![An Excel sheet with a grouped table](../reference/figures/excel.webp)

## PowerPoint

`phw_pptx()` starts a 16:9 deck from the bundled PHW template, with Ubuntu
text and navy titles. Pass your organisation's PowerPoint template to use
its slide layouts instead. `phw_add_slide()` adds a slide with a styled title and a
chart, table or bullet points. Charts are editable in PowerPoint when the
rvg package is installed.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
deck <- phw_pptx() |>
  phw_add_slide("Key messages", text = c("First message", "Second message")) |>
  phw_add_slide("Grouped table", table = tab, source = "Example data") |>
  phw_add_slide("A chart", plot = ggplot(dat, aes(group)) + geom_bar(), source = "Example data")
print(deck, target = "slides.pptx")
```

![Three PowerPoint slides](../reference/figures/powerpoint.webp)

Give a chart or table `alt` text so screen readers can describe it, and
use `caption_args` for any `phw_caption()` argument other than `source` and
`date`. Without `alt`, a chart takes the text from `labs(alt = )`.
`phw_reference_pptx()` writes the template to a file, to open in PowerPoint
or to pass to another tool.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
deck <- phw_pptx() |>
  phw_add_slide("Cases by group", plot = ggplot(dat, aes(group)) + geom_bar(),
                alt = "Bar chart of cases in groups A, B and C.",
                source = "Example data", caption_args = list(source_prefix = "Data: "))
phw_reference_pptx("phw-template.pptx")
```

## Word

Any `phw_flextable()` can be saved to Word, several to one file:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
flextable::save_as_docx(`Table 1` = phw_flextable(tab), path = "tables.docx")
```

For whole reports, use `output: phwstyle::phw_word_document` in R Markdown
or `format: phw-docx` in Quarto: see [Reports and documents](documents.html).

## Interactive tables

`phw_datatable()` gives a searchable, sortable, paged table for long lists.

```{r, eval = requireNamespace("DT", quietly = TRUE)}
phw_datatable(dat, caption = "Grouped table", source = "Example data", filter = "top")
```
